# Tobit Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_004_page_001.jpg

---

**1** On that day Tobit remembered the money he had deposited with Gabael in Rages of Media,

**2** and he said to himself, "I have prayed for death — why then do I not call my son Tobias and tell him about this money before I die?"

**3** So he called him and said: "My son, when I die, give me a proper burial, and do not dishonor your mother. Honor her all the days of your life; do what pleases her, and do not cause her grief.

**4** Remember, my son, that she faced many dangers for your sake when she carried you in the womb. When she dies, bury her beside me in the same tomb.

**5** All your days, my son, keep the Lord our God in mind, and refuse to sin or transgress his commandments. Practice righteousness all the days of your life, and do not walk in the paths of wrongdoing.

**6** For if you act in truth, your deeds will prosper — as they do for all who practice righteousness.

**7** Give alms from your possessions, and do not let your eye be grudging when you give alms. Do not turn your face away from any poor person, and God will not turn his face from you.

**8** Give alms in proportion to what you have. If you have much, give more; if you have little, do not be afraid to give according to that little.

**9** For in so doing you are storing up a good treasure for yourself against a day of necessity.

**10** For almsgiving delivers from death and prevents a man from going down into the darkness.

**11** Almsgiving is a great offering of confidence before the Most High for all who practice it.

**12** Beware of all fornication, my son. Above all, take a wife from the descendants of your fathers — do not take a foreign wife, one who is not of your father's tribe. For we are sons of the prophets. Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, our fathers of old — remember, my son, that all of them married women from among their own kindred, and they were blessed in their children, and their descendants will inherit the land.

**13** And now, my son, love your kindred, and do not be proud in your heart toward your brothers and sisters, the sons and daughters of your people, in taking a wife from among them. For in pride there is ruin and great instability, and in laziness there is poverty and want — for idleness is the mother of famine.

**14** Do not let the wages of any man who works for you remain with you overnight; pay him at once. And if you serve God, you will be recompensed. Be careful, my son, in all your deeds, and show good discipline in all your conduct.

**15** What you hate, do not do to anyone. Do not drink wine to excess, and do not let drunkenness be your traveling companion.

**16** Share your bread with the hungry, and give your clothing to the naked. From all your abundance give alms, and do not let your eye begrudge the giving.

**17** Spread your bread on the grave of the righteous, but do not give to sinners.

**18** Seek counsel from every wise person, and do not despise any useful advice.

**19** At all times bless the Lord God, and ask him to direct your paths and make your counsels and plans succeed. For no nation possesses wisdom of itself, but the Lord himself gives every good thing. He humbles whomever he wills, just as he wills. So now, my son, keep my commandments in mind and do not let them fade from your heart.

**20** Let me tell you now about the ten talents of silver I deposited with Gabael son of Gabrias at Rages in Media.

**21** Do not be afraid, my son, because we have become poor. You have great wealth if you fear God, and flee from every sin, and do what is good in the sight of the Lord your God.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **eleēmosynē** (vv. 7–11, 16): Rendered "alms" / "almsgiving" throughout. The Greek term covers charitable giving with covenantal overtones. LOGOS chose "alms" as the most formal English equivalent; "mercy-gift" was considered but less natural.
- **v. 12**: "descendants of your fathers" — more natural than "seed of your fathers" while maintaining genealogical force. The patriarchal list (Noah–Abraham–Isaac–Jacob) is retained in full per Sinaiticus.
- **v. 15**: "What you hate, do not do to anyone" — the negative Golden Rule is preserved verbatim. No modernization attempted. This phrasing predates its NT positive form (Matt 7:12) by centuries.
- **v. 17**: "Spread your bread" — the Greek *ekcheai* (pour/spread) describes placing food at gravesites of the righteous, a Jewish mourning custom. Retained rather than normalized to "offer."
- **v. 19**: "no nation possesses wisdom of itself" — formal rendering of the Greek *ou pasa ethnos boulēn echei*; preserves the theological claim that wisdom comes only from God.
- **v. 6**: "act in truth" — retained over "be honest" or "live faithfully" to preserve the Greek *alētheia* (truth) as a comprehensive term for covenant integrity. — LOGOS
